title: [-1B] FrankenMTP acceptance primitives + break-even alpha*(SKU)
description:
[-1B] FrankenMTP acceptance-surface primitives + break-even curve alpha*(SKU).

WHAT: measure the primitives of the expected-case FrankenMTP cost model T(alpha) = T_draft + T_verify + (1 - alpha_full) * T_repair: T_verify (the seq-16 block pass at real shapes — from the W8A8 bench + a prototype verify kernel), T_repair variants (sequential suffix; re-draft+re-verify), and candidate T_draft costs (prev-frame copy + transition stats; small-head drafts). Publish the BREAK-EVEN ACCEPTANCE CURVE alpha*(SKU): the acceptance rate above which speculation beats pure sequential on each target.

WHY (v2.1 hardness fix): the high-acceptance asymptote (~0.55 GB/frame, sequential-baseline 103 GB/s at 5x dropping to mid-30s) is a CEILING, not a plan — partial accepts at depth k can be WORSE than pure sequential (draft + full verify + residual sequential all paid). Without alpha*, FrankenMTP cannot be honestly ranked against hot-packing and Q4. Real drafter acceptance alpha is measured later (3A) — THIS bead makes the target concrete before the drafter exists.

DONE WHEN: T-primitive measurements + the alpha*(SKU) curves committed; the 3A FrankenMTP bead's keep/revert gate references these curves.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-5, AzureThrush] CLAIM TIER VERDICT: **TIER 1** -- the training-mode causal forward IS mask- and distribution-equivalent to the 15-step sequential inference loop. Exact-verifier claims are LICENSED. Full line-cited derivation: docs/truth-pack/OQ5_MICRODECODER_WIRING.md.

The index map you must implement (identical in both paths, proven executably by scripts/oq5_index_equivalence.py):
  pos 0        = talker hidden state (conditioning, NOT scored)
  pos 1        = TALKER codec embedding (vocab 3072) of c0  -> lm_head[0]   -> c1
  pos 2..15    = code_predictor.codec_embedding[p-2] (vocab 2048) of c_{p-1} -> lm_head[p-1] -> c_p
Mask: plain 16x16 lower-triangular causal, positions 0..15, no sliding (all 5 layer_types are full_attention, sliding_window null). Rotary: plain RoPE theta 1e6, no scaling.

TWO TRAPS, both of which silently invalidate the epic:
1. Position 1 is SCORED. Plan §7.5's phrasing ('one conditioning/primary position plus 15 residual positions') reads as though c0's slot were unscored; it is not. Count is right, head placement is easy to get one off.
2. Position 1's embedding comes from the TALKER's table, not a code_predictor table.

NUMERICAL CAVEAT (see docs/truth-pack/OQ5_MICRODECODER_WIRING.md §6): equivalence is exact in exact arithmetic. A seq-16 batched matmul and 15 m=1 GEMVs may differ in reduction order / last ULPs. Strict-mode acceptance must compare ARGMAX/token ids, not logit bits, unless the verify kernel reproduces the sequential reduction order exactly. Ledger a DISCREPANCIES entry when the verify kernel lands.

HONESTY NOTE: this verdict is [VERIFIED-STATIC] (line-level reading of pinned source + pinned config). Numeric oracle confirmation is frankentts-m1u, blocked on the oracle env. If m1u ever contradicts this, the Tier-1 verdict re-opens and this comment is wrong.

title: [-1B] Costed execution graph generator (sequential baseline + one-read floor)
description:
[-1B] The costed execution graph generator (scripts/cost_model.py -> docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md core).

WHAT: from the pinned spec + census, generate a per-op table: component, layer, residual depth (where applicable), shape, dtype, executions per audio frame, weight bytes, activation bytes, MACs, KV bytes read/written, predicted cache level, parallel dimension, kernel candidates. The report explicitly contains: talker cost/frame (~443 MB Q8 incl. primary head); EACH of the 15 microdecoder depths; total serial depth (12.5x28=350 talker-layer + 12.5x15x5=937.5 microdecoder-layer evals/sec); codec cost per 1- and 4-frame packet; x-vector and ICL prefill costs; cold text-embedding row traffic; max KV by duration; single- and N-stream traffic lower bounds.

CRITICAL LABELING (v2.1 hardness fix): the ~1.65 GB/frame table is the SEQUENTIAL-EXECUTION BASELINE, not a physics floor — the all-components one-read floor is ~0.55 GB/frame (~6.9 GB/s at 1x). Never let the 20.7 GB/s figure be quoted as the bound "even after" residency/speculation levers. Both numbers appear side by side in every output.

WHY: this graph is what re-ranks the hot-op table per profile, prices the FrankenMTP-vs-hot-pack composition per SKU, and sets honest G2 targets. It is the bakeoff Gate-B input too.

DONE WHEN: generator committed + reproducible from pinned inputs alone; report reviewed against the traffic arithmetic in the plan (440/78.6x15/31.5/1.65 GB chain); consumed by the -1B experiment beads.

title: [-1B] G2 targets + roofline factors (PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md)
description:
[-1B] Set numeric G2 targets + roofline-efficiency factors (PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md complete).

WHAT: consolidate all -1B outputs into docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md (a LIVING document thereafter) answering the seven feasibility questions: (1) microdecoder cache-residency per SKU; (2) which hardware tier limits 1x/2x/5x RT; (3) W8A8-vs-W8A16 winners per shape; (4) the stream count where batched GEMM overtakes per-stream GEMV; (5) codec-overlap help-vs-contention; (6) is 5x RT on M4 plausible WITHOUT speculative MTP or Q4; (7) break-even acceptance alpha*(SKU). Then set the NUMERIC G2 targets: per-stage TTFA + RTF vs the proven baseline (interactive profile); aggregate RTF/socket + streams/socket + p95 queueing + joules/min (throughput profile); and the ROOFLINE-EFFICIENCY FACTORS (each hot stage within a stated factor of its floor, per SKU) — the structural claim that certifies the thesis, beyond beating incumbents.

WHY: until this exists, ALL speed numbers are hypotheses (standing stretch: first packet <=~200 ms warm, >=5x RT single-stream on M4-class — published per-SKU honestly if the roofline says otherwise). Also re-ranks the hot-op table per profile (the a-priori ranking is explicitly provisional).

DONE WHEN: the doc committed; seven questions answered with measurement citations; G2 target table + roofline factors adopted into the success-metrics tracking; hot-op ranking re-issued per profile.

title: [-1B] Instrument official + MLX/GGML per stage (proven baseline)
description:
[-1B] Instrument the official + MLX/GGML implementations per stage.

WHAT: stage-level wall-clock + memory instrumentation of (a) the pinned official stack and (b) the best community MLX and GGML ports, measuring SEPARATELY: talker step alone; EVERY microdecoder depth individually; the 15 microdecoder steps as a unit; codec packet decode (1- and 4-frame); prompt preparation + prefill (both clone modes); ECAPA + codec encoders. On each target SKU class (M4-class Apple, high-core AMD, baseline x86).

WHY: (a) establishes the PROVEN CPU baseline for G2 (per OQ-15's verdict on which implementation legitimately runs); (b) reveals where generic-runtime overhead actually sits (the thesis predicts the microdecoder's 15 small steps drown in HF generation machinery — verify, don't assume); (c) provides the reference profiles for bakeoff Gate B; (d) anchors the roofline-efficiency factors (measured distance from the cost-graph floors).

FAIRNESS: pinned incumbent contract (never "whatever sat at that path that day"); thread parity; interleaved thermal pairing per OQ-17's method; cv%>5 refuses the row.

DONE WHEN: per-stage tables committed for all three implementations x target SKUs with the full fairness metadata; rows feed PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: [-1B] Metal microdecoder spike (go/no-go)
description:
[-1B] Metal microdecoder feasibility spike (one narrow question, answered cheaply).

THE QUESTION: can a persistent Metal kernel or command-graph execute the 15 residual microdecoder steps — INCLUDING per-depth sampling and KV updates — without 15 host round trips?

WHY NOW (moved from Phase 6 to -1B): a positive answer makes the microdecoder vastly more attractive on M5 and constrains artifact/quant layout choices to stay Metal-compatible (discovering late that the layouts were wrong for the strongest Apple path is the failure this spike prevents); a negative answer closes the path CHEAPLY with a documented verdict. Metal PRODUCTIZATION stays Phase 6 (with its pre-stated full-path contract: integer cross-backend int8xint8->i32 exactness, talker/codec co-residency, CPU-fallback invariants). Evidence context: M5-class fused INT8 Metal precedent exists (Draw Things: 1.61-1.87x over FP16 matmul; INT8 attention 1.24-1.41x over Metal FlashAttention — mechanism proof, not our targets).

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: a spike — throwaway code, go/no-go doc as the deliverable, timeboxed; a negative verdict is a VALID outcome recorded in NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

DONE WHEN: go/no-go document committed with measured round-trip counts + prototype timings; Phase-6 epic annotated with the verdict.

title: [-1B] Packet-size experiments (TTFA vs overhead)
description:
[-1B] Packet-size experiments (1/2/4-frame codec packets).

WHAT: measure, on the reference implementations (and later our codec), TTFA and steady-state cost as a function of codec packet size (1, 2, 4 frames): first-audible-sample latency, per-packet scheduling overhead, cache behavior of packet-batched codec decode.

WHY: the official system uses 4-frame 320 ms packets to amortize scheduling overhead, but OUR dispatch-free runtime may make 1-2-frame packets (80-160 ms lower first-audio latency) cheap — packet size is an execution-policy parameter mapped to profiles (interactive->1-2, balanced->4, throughput->larger, strict->conformance packetization), and this experiment supplies the numbers behind the mapping + the packet-frames auto policy.

DONE WHEN: packet-size curves per SKU committed; the profile->packet default mapping justified from data; strict-mode packetization defined per OQ-14.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from OQ-14, docs/QWEN3_TTS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md sec 3-4] Packet definition + TTFA protocol:
 * 1 packet = 4 code frames = 320 ms = 7680 samples @ 24 kHz (paper sec 4, 12 Hz rate). This is a
   PAPER definition -- the released code has no packetization at all, so there is nothing to imitate;
   correctness is validated by the streaming==batch invariant instead.
 * TTFA protocol: report TTFA and RTF separately; pin TTFA = (talker prefill + 4 frames of nested
   decode) + (codec decode of those 4 frames), reporting the two addends separately so a regression
   can be attributed (mirrors the paper's LM-TTFP / tokenizer-TPP split). Hold non_streaming_mode
   CONSTANT across comparisons -- prefill dominates TTFA and the two geometries differ by the whole
   text length. Report per packet size (1/2/4).
 * Upstream reference row (Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B, concurrency 1): LM TTFP 93 ms + tokenizer 4 ms =
   97 ms first-packet, LM TPP 19 ms, RTF 0.288. NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO against it -- measured on an
   unnamed 'single typical computational resource' with an internal vLLM engine. Use it only as a
   documented upstream claim, never as a head-to-head baseline.

title: [OQ-18/-1B] Cache-residency under talker interference (per SKU)
description:
[OQ-18 / -1B] Cache-residency experiments: the hot working set UNDER TALKER INTERFERENCE.

THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES 3A's SHAPE: does the ~110 MB-class Q8 microdecoder hot working set (exact bytes from OQ-2) stay resident in the outermost cache between its 15 immediate reuses per frame — ON EACH TARGET SKU — given that the ~440 MB talker weight stream runs between microdecoder bursts every frame? "Does 110 MB fit in L3/SLC?" is NOT the question; "does it SURVIVE talker eviction across the real talker->microdecoder->codec schedule?" is.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITION (v2.1 — residency is a measured quantity, not a vibe): measured DRAM bytes/frame for the microdecoder sections (PMCs on x86, Instruments/powermetrics counters on Apple) approaching the one-read floor (~110 MB/frame), with body-tile hit rates as the diagnostic. FAILS CLEANLY when DRAM bytes/frame stay near the sequential baseline (~1.2 GB/frame) despite packing.

METHOD: synthetic kernels replaying the real access pattern (from the cost graph) before any real engine exists; per-SKU sweep (M4/M5 SLC, AMD L3-per-CCD, Intel). Output: per-SKU residency verdict + the eviction-pressure curve.

WHY: if residency holds, 3A's hot pack is a layout problem and FrankenMTP's win is serial latency; if it fails, FrankenMTP is the traffic lever and the failure-mode playbook (Q4 depth waterfall, prefetch injection, CCD pinning) activates. The two flagship levers are partial substitutes — this experiment prices them per SKU.

DONE WHEN: per-SKU verdict table committed with counter methodology; consumed by the 3A hot-pack and FrankenMTP beads.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from exec-census-drift-dx5, docs/truth-pack/EXECUTION_CENSUS.json] YOUR RESIDENCY TARGET IS BIGGER
THAN THE PLAN SAYS. Derived from the pinned tensor shapes, not estimated:

  5-layer body            78.7 MB Q8   (plan 2.6 said ~79 -- exact)
  15 per-depth embeddings 31.5 MB Q8   (plan lists these, then omits them from its own total)
  15 per-depth heads      31.5 MB Q8   (plan said 31.5 -- exact)
  + KV (320 KiB) + RoPE table
  = HOT WORKING SET 142.2 MB Q8, not the '~110 MB-class' in plan 2.6.

79 + 31.5 = 110.5 is body + heads only. The per-depth embeddings are a real, separate 31.5 MB that
must also stay resident across the 15 reuses, so the number your experiment has to test against is
142.2 MB. That is ~29% more, and it is exactly the range where an SLC either does or does not hold
it -- so this changes the question, not just the constant.

Per-frame traffic is 1.24 GB (body reread 15x + embeddings and heads once), consistent with plan
2.6's accounting.

The census is regenerated from pinned inputs and guarded against drift in check.sh, so if a re-pin
changes any of this your experiment's target moves with it rather than silently going stale.

title: [-1B] W8A8 vs W8A16 vs BF16 microbenchmarks (KernelPlan seed)
description:
[-1B] W8A8 vs W8A16 vs BF16 microbenchmarks at the real shapes.

WHAT: for each op class x ISA, benchmark weight-int8+activation-int8 (dynamic per-row quant), weight-int8+activation-bf16/f16 (weight-only), and BF16/F16 baseline, at THE REAL SHAPES: single-row talker GEMV (1024->2048, 2048->1024, 1024->3072, 3072->1024); microdecoder step GEMV (same family); the seq-16 verification block pass; text-prefill GEMM (long m); codec conv shapes (hidden 512); multi-stream batched GEMM (m = 2..64).

WHY (v2.1: the frankentorch int8 linear is the INCUMBENT, not the assumed winner): the winner plausibly differs per regime — dynamic activation quant costs a pass over activations, which m=1 GEMV may not amortize, while batched GEMM usually does. The results seed the KernelPlan autotuner's search space and the Phase-2 decision of which quant execution modes to wire. ISA selection is per (shape, regime) — NO fixed AMX > AVX-512 > AVX-VNNI hierarchy (AMX is excellent for big tiles, poor at batch-one GEMV).

DONE WHEN: winner table per (op class x ISA x m) committed with cv% metadata; fed into KernelPlan design + PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: [BAKE] Bakeoff corpus + powered judging protocol
description:
[BAKE] Build the bakeoff corpus + judging protocol.

WHAT: the full-strength evaluation corpus (distinct from the conformance golden corpus): 50-100 speakers; 3/10/30-second references; clean-studio, ordinary-phone, reverberant-room, and noisy conditions; ordinary prose, dialogue, numbers, currencies, names, acronyms, URLs, quotations, long sentences; emotional and neutral delivery; same-language and cross-language cloning. Judging protocol per the operationalized listening design: ABX speaker-identity (reference A, candidates B/C), pairwise/MUSHRA-style naturalness, TOST equivalence bounds with predefined margins, hierarchical analysis over speaker/text/language/listener, tail reporting on canary axes.

WHY: several hundred blind pairwise judgments per serious comparison — but POWERED and correctly grouped, not undifferentiated. This corpus serves Gate A now and quantization/listening gates later. All reference audio must be consent-clean (doctrine 10).

DONE WHEN: corpus assembled with manifests + provenance; judge protocol doc committed (effect sizes, margins, power analysis owner); dry-run with a small listener pool validates the pipeline.
close_reason: Corpus compiler, text corpus, judging protocol and dry-run delivered. SCOPE STATEMENT, read this before assuming completeness: the AUDIO half is deliberately NOT in this bead and is tracked as frankentts-bsz, which now blocks Gate A. Delivered: corpus/bakeoff/texts.json (100 authored texts, 11 categories, en/zh/es/ja + code-switching, every design.toml category minimum met); corpus/bakeoff/design.toml (the coverage contract, per-cell minima derived from the listening power analysis); scripts/bakeoff/{corpus,build_corpus}.py (coverage + consent validation, stimulus emitter, dry-run) with three-way exit codes that never conflate a coverage shortfall with a consent blocker; docs/BAKEOFF_CORPUS.md. Judging protocol is the bakeoff_gate_a instance in scripts/listening/margins.toml — effect sizes, margins, power analysis and named owner reused from frankentts-v-listening-25m rather than re-invented. Consent (doctrine 10) is enforced in code: six required fields, a closed set of permitted scopes, named forbidden scopes, and one incomplete row blocks the WHOLE corpus. DRY-RUN MET and two-sided: 634 stimulus items, 156 complete cells, 0 dropped; a 32-listener panel reaches PASS with design_valid pass, an 8-listener panel is correctly REFUSED as INVALID. Synthetic panel, is_quality_claim false — validates the corpus->panel seam, says nothing about audio. Design findings: a panel must hold reference length constant (the harness keys cells on speaker x text x language x regime, so mixing 3s and 30s confounds the system contrast — now a hard error), and Tier-0 objective metrics must span all reference buckets, not just the panel's. The validator's invisible-character rule caught two real defects in my own authoring: a soft hyphen inside a surname and a stray Thai character in a Japanese sentence. 'build_corpus.py validate' currently exits 2 (NOT READY) naming exactly one reason: no reference recordings.

title: [BAKE] Gate A: upstream quality bakeoff
description:
[BAKE] Gate A — upstream quality (official implementations only).

WHAT: run the four contestants on the bakeoff corpus using their OFFICIAL implementations (no franken code): Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base (champion), Pocket TTS 100M (challenger), Chatterbox Turbo 350M, MOSS-TTS-Nano 100M; Qwen3-TTS 1.7B as upper-bound reference ONLY. Measure: identity, naturalness, prosody/accent retention, intelligibility/WER, hallucinations/repeats/skips/premature endings, reference-noise leakage, long-form drift, multilingual behavior, enrollment sensitivity; plus cold start, enrollment time, warm TTFA, RTF, memory, energy (per OQ-17 method).

DECISION RULE: Pocket is ELIMINATED as primary if it fails a PREDECLARED quality floor (identity equivalence bound vs Qwen on the intended workload — its published -114 Elo speaker-similarity deficit vs Chatterbox is the prior reason it is challenger). Chatterbox/MOSS anchor the field. Speaker-embedding cosine computed with multiple unrelated encoders and treated as SECONDARY to human judgments.

WHY UPSTREAM-ONLY: decouples model quality from implementation maturity; needs none of our code so it runs in parallel with -1A/-1B.

DONE WHEN: scorecards + verdict committed under docs/bakeoff/; the quality floor decision recorded BEFORE unblinding (precommitted).

title: [BAKE] Gate B: architectural systems potential + isomorphism map
description:
[BAKE] Gate B — architectural systems potential (cost-model comparison, no ports).

WHAT: using the -1B cost model + reference profiles + representative microbenchmarks: exact op counts for both architectures, cache-fit models, footprints, rooflines — organized around an explicit STAGE ISOMORPHISM MAP (Qwen <-> Pocket): text/prefill <-> text/prefill; 28-layer talker backbone <-> 6-layer generator backbone; 15-step residual microdecoder <-> one-step consistency frame head; RVQ codec decoder <-> 20M causal VAE; streaming <-> streaming. Pocket facts for the model: ~90M generator + 20M VAE, continuous VAE frames (no discrete residual loop!), 12.5 fps, upstream-measured ~6x RT on two M4 CPU cores, ~200 ms first chunk, no batch-one GPU advantage (CPU-only path).

DECISION: does Pocket's structure (notably: NO 15x microdecoder reread problem at all) justify parallel systems investment? Answered WITHOUT pretending either side is "equivalently optimized" — that was the v1 kill rule's circularity, now fixed.

DONE WHEN: isomorphism map + comparative systems dossier committed; go/no-go on the Gate-C timeboxed Pocket path recorded.

title: [BAKE] Gate C: optimized confirmation (final champion decision)
description:
[BAKE] Gate C — optimized confirmation + final champion decision.

WHAT: with the champion's 3A microdecoder/talker path and the timeboxed Pocket core path both existing, run the final quality/performance decision on the bakeoff corpus under full fairness controls.

THE DECISION RULE (precommitted): displacement requires BOTH (a) Pocket retains >= ~95% of Qwen's human-preference rate on speaker identity + naturalness on the intended workload AND (b) >= 2x end-to-end systems advantage after the representative optimization. Failing EITHER, Qwen stays champion. Real-time speech does not become more useful at 20x real time if it sounds like the wrong person — identity dominates.

OUTCOMES: (1) Qwen confirmed -> Pocket track closes with a ledger entry; (2) Pocket displaces -> champion swap (a project-level decision with massive re-planning, deliberately made expensive); (3) MIXED -> dual-engine product hard-required (see the timeboxed-path bead). Whatever the verdict: recorded with full evidence in docs/bakeoff/, and the Phase-3 entry evidence updated.

DONE WHEN: verdict + evidence committed; downstream beads (Phase-5 zoo track or closure entries) filed accordingly.

title: [BAKE] Timeboxed Pocket core path (Gate-C evidence)
description:
[BAKE] Timeboxed representative Pocket core path (Gate-C prerequisite; runs ONLY if Gates A+B pass).

WHAT: a TIMEBOXED, scope-bounded optimized implementation of Pocket's core loop (the Gate-B isomorphism map defines which stages are "representative" — likely the 6-layer generator step + consistency head + VAE decode), sufficient to make an honest optimized-vs-optimized comparison against our 3A microdecoder/talker path. EXPLICITLY NOT a second full port — the timebox bounds DECISION EVIDENCE.

COMMITMENT CARRIED FROM THE PLAN: if Gate C returns a MIXED verdict (Pocket wins some regimes, e.g. ultra-edge), the dual-engine product is HARD-REQUIRED — Pocket onboarded as the ultra-edge profile inside the same CLI via the governing skill's full add-model recipe (additive ModelArch with the Qwen exemplar as impl #1 under a zero-regression gate), with COMPLETE certification. The timebox never certifies a shipping engine.

DONE WHEN: the representative path exists with its own mini parity checks vs Pocket's official implementation; measured numbers comparable under the same fairness controls as ours.

title: [BAKE] Collect consent-clean bakeoff reference audio (50-100 speakers)
description:
Collect the AUDIO half of the bakeoff corpus. The text half (100 texts, 11 categories, 4 languages + code-switching) and the whole corpus compiler landed under frankentts-bake-corpus-48h; `python3 scripts/bakeoff/build_corpus.py validate` currently exits 2 (NOT READY) naming exactly one reason: no reference recordings.

WHAT: populate corpus/bakeoff/speakers.json and corpus/bakeoff/references.json to the contract in corpus/bakeoff/design.toml — >=50 speakers (target 100), >=8 per language across en/zh/es/ja; 3s/10s/30s reference buckets with >=40 speakers per bucket and >=2 buckets per speaker; clean_studio / ordinary_phone / reverberant_room / noisy each >=12 speakers; neutral and emotional delivery each >=12 speakers; >=6 cross-language (reference, target) pairs.

CONSENT (doctrine 10, enforced in code): every reference row needs consent_statement, consent_obtained_utc, consent_scope, speaker_pseudonym, provenance, sha256. consent_scope must be one of explicit_recorded_for_this_project / licensed_dataset_with_speaker_consent / public_domain_with_documented_consent. scraped/web_harvested/assumed/implied/unknown are rejected by name. One incomplete row blocks the WHOLE corpus (exit 1) — there is no partial-credit mode.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD: this is a human recruitment-and-attestation process, not a coding task. An agent must not acquire voices, and this project ships no audio-acquisition features. The compiler, schema, and refusal behaviour are already built and waiting.

DONE WHEN: build_corpus.py validate exits 0 (READY for Gate A); the dry-run path (already proven end-to-end with synthetic records) runs against real audio.

title: [P2] mmap loader + madvise application of the .fttsq page-in policy (audited unsafe island)
description:
Split out of frankentts-p2-fttsq-format-wsa, which landed the DECISION layer and closed on it.

WHAT EXISTS (crates/ftts-artifacts/src/fttsq.rs, committed 65bb84f):
  PagePolicy { Resident, LazyRowGranular, OnDemand }
  AccessClass::page_policy() -> PagePolicy       // total, pure, unit-tested
  PagePolicy::may_prefetch() -> bool             // the MADV_WILLNEED predicate
  FttsqReader::page_in_plan() -> Vec<(&SectionEntry, PagePolicy)>
      // resident first, smallest-first within the resident group, so the ~110 MB microdecoder
      // pack is prefetched ahead of the ~4x larger talker and wins the cache race
Tests already pin the invariants: COLD_TEXT_EMBEDDING never prefetches; is_hot()/is_row_granular()
can never disagree with page_policy().

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES: apply that plan. mmap the artifact, then issue the madvise matching each
section's PagePolicy, and hand the runtime a borrowed view over the mapping.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD, not scope-creep on the format: ftts-artifacts is forbid(unsafe_code)
and a forbid cannot be lowered by allow (AGENTS.md Toolchain). mmap/madvise therefore MUST live in
ftts-kernels, the one crate permitted audited unsafe -- a cross-crate change with its own SAFETY
notes, its own scalar/portable fallback, and its own platform matrix. Bundling it into the format
bead would have blocked the parser surface that v-fuzzing-sn0 and the converter are waiting on.

DONE WHEN:
  - mmap island in ftts-kernels: named feature-gated module, every unsafe load carrying a
    // SAFETY: note, per AGENTS.md.
  - Each section gets the madvise implied by its PagePolicy. An assertion (not a comment) that
    !policy.may_prefetch() sections are NEVER passed MADV_WILLNEED -- the 622 MB cold embedding
    is the case that matters and the one a refactor would silently break.
  - Platform matrix: madvise flags differ (Linux MADV_WILLNEED/MADV_RANDOM vs macOS; Windows has
    no madvise -- decide PrefetchVirtualMemory or documented no-op). Must compile on all five
    release targets, per the CI cross matrix.
  - Row-granular access for COLD_TEXT_EMBEDDING actually exercised: fetch a single embedding row
    without faulting the section in wholesale. This is the one that needs a real measurement, not
    just a call -- assert resident-page count or measured fault count, else "never WILLNEEDed"
    stays an untested claim.
  - A measurement, not an assertion, that residency behaves: DRAM bytes/frame or page-fault counts
    per access class. Feeds OQ-18.

DEPENDS ON: frankentts-p2-fttsq-format-wsa (closed -- policy layer + page_in_plan()).
close_reason: residency advice applied and measured pre-digest; per-row fault avoidance NOT provable under v1 eager digest — deferred to frankentts-fttsq-v2-page-granular-integrity-mhl

comments.text: STATUS 2026-08-06: loader application landed in commits 6d52934 (MappedFttsq applies PagePolicy, records advice plus mincore observations) and f4d046a/a35ea26 (feature-gated POSIX mmap/madvise/mincore island with safe fallback). The cold embedding is asserted never to receive MADV_WILLNEED; its row access is exercised. BLOCKER TO CLOSE: v1 FttsqReader verifies each section SHA-256 eagerly before a mapping is exposed, necessarily reading the whole cold section. The recorded pre-digest residency is a measurement hook, but cannot prove a single cold row avoids wholesale faults. A page-granular integrity format (for example Merkle/chunk digests) is required for the bead’s requested row-fault and DRAM/page-fault measurement. title: EPIC Bakeoff: three sequential gates (champion validation)
description:
EPIC — Bakeoff: three sequential gates validating the champion choice (Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base) against challenger Kyutai Pocket TTS 100M.

WHY THREE GATES: the original single kill rule ("Pocket wins if >=2x systems advantage after equivalent optimization") was CIRCULAR — it demanded optimization evidence before optimization exists. Fix: Gate A (upstream quality, official implementations only — Pocket eliminated if it fails a predeclared identity/naturalness floor vs Qwen; its published Elo deficit is -114 vs Chatterbox on speaker similarity, which is WHY it is challenger not champion); Gate B (architectural systems potential from the -1B cost model + microbenchmarks, organized around an explicit stage isomorphism map: text/prefill <-> text/prefill, talker backbone <-> Pocket backbone, microdecoder <-> consistency frame head, RVQ codec <-> causal VAE, streaming <-> streaming — so continuous-frame vs discrete-16-group comparison is structural, not rhetorical); Gate C (optimized confirmation ONLY if A and B pass: displacement requires BOTH >=~95% human-preference retention on identity+naturalness AND >=2x end-to-end systems advantage; failing either, Qwen stays champion).

IMPORTANT COMMITMENTS: Gate C's Pocket path is timeboxed/representative — the timebox bounds DECISION EVIDENCE only; a mixed verdict (Pocket wins some regimes) HARD-REQUIRES the dual-engine product (Pocket as ultra-edge profile in the same CLI) via the skill's full add-model recipe with complete certification. Qwen3-TTS 1.7B serves as upper-bound quality reference only. Artifacts live under docs/bakeoff/. Gates A+B verdicts are Phase-3 entry evidence.

title: EPIC Phase -1A: Exact Model Truth (truth pack + oracle)
description:
EPIC — Phase -1A: Exact Model Truth (truth pack + oracle). THE FOUNDATION: no kernel ships until its per-component gates are green.

CONTEXT: franken_tts is a pure-Rust, memory-safe, CPU-hyper-optimized library + single-binary CLI (ftts) running Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base (zero-shot voice-cloning TTS; Apache-2.0 pending OQ-1 verification) with NO general ML framework, per the /ai-model-into-rust-mega-fused-hyper-kernel doctrine. Project thesis: the model hides a 15-step autoregressive Residual-Code Microdecoder inside every 80 ms frame (28-layer talker once -> 5-layer microdecoder x15 SEQUENTIAL -> causal codec decode), ~1.65 GB Q8 weight traffic per frame on the sequential baseline (~20.7 GB/s at 1x real time). We turn that microdecoder from the model's largest CPU liability into its largest optimization advantage: cache-resident hot-packing, per-depth quantization, and FrankenMTP speculative block verification.

WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS: every architectural fact currently carries a [SOURCE] tag (read from the LIVE official repo/configs during plan review; URLs in plan v2.1 section 17) or [REPORTED]. Plan v1 shipped a load-bearing architecture error (missed the 15x microdecoder loop) precisely because facts were unpinned. This epic pins + hashes every source, promotes/corrects every fact, resolves OQ-1..OQ-17, extracts docs/QWEN3_TTS_EXECUTABLE_SPEC.md, and stands up the reference oracle + its measured nondeterminism floor (oracle BEFORE engine — the governing skill's Phase 0 lives here, assigned explicitly so it cannot fall through the cracks).

GATING POLICY (v2.1): truth gating is PER-COMPONENT — a kernel is blocked only by the unresolved OQs it depends on; a watermark question does not block a verified talker GEMV.

EXIT: per-component truth gates green for talker, microdecoder, codec, encoders, prompt builder; oracle fixtures + committed nondeterminism-floor envelope; executable spec committed.

title: EPIC Phase -1B: Cost and Feasibility Model
description:
EPIC — Phase -1B: Cost & Feasibility Model (the v2 centerpiece; runs after/alongside -1A, before ANY heroic kernel work).

WHY: v1 promised speed numbers before understanding the machine. The corrected traffic model shows ~1.65 GB/frame sequential baseline (~20.7 GB/s at 1x RT; the microdecoder body alone is ~1.18 GB/frame reread 15x). Whether targets like 5x-RT-on-M4 are even physically plausible depends on measurements nobody has yet: cache residency of the ~110 MB-class microdecoder hot working set UNDER talker interference, W8A8-vs-W8A16 winners at real shapes, packet-size behavior, and the FrankenMTP acceptance-surface primitives. Until this epic completes, ALL speed numbers are hypotheses, never promises (G2 policy).

CONTENT: a generated costed execution graph (per-op: component, layer, residual depth, shape, dtype, executions/frame, weight/activation/KV bytes, MACs, predicted cache level, parallel dim, kernel candidates); instrumentation of the official + MLX/GGML implementations per stage; per-SKU memory-hierarchy measurements; the Metal microdecoder spike; the seven feasibility questions incl. break-even acceptance alpha*(SKU); bakeoff Gate A concludes + Gate B runs here.

EXIT: all seven questions answered with measurements; docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md committed; numeric G2 targets + roofline-efficiency factors set; the section-7.1 hot-op ranking re-ranked from data per profile.

title: EPIC Phase 0: Minimal executable skeleton (workspace)
description:
EPIC — Phase 0: Minimal executable skeleton. The workspace compiles end-to-end empty on all 5 targets before any model code exists.

SHAPE (load-bearing, fixes a v1 compile-impossibility): a forbid(unsafe_code) lint CANNOT be locally allow-ed in Rust, so the single-crate-with-unsafe-islands design does not compile. Instead: tiny workspace under crates/ — ftts-core (engine/orchestrator/KernelTeam protocol/streaming queues/robot events/audio+text front ends; forbid unsafe), ftts-model-qwen (talker/microdecoder/sampler/codec/speaker/prompt; forbid unsafe), ftts-artifacts (all artifact parsers + streaming converter; forbid unsafe), ftts-kernels (THE ONLY crate permitting audited unsafe, in named feature-gated islands with SAFETY comments + bit-identical scalar fallbacks; the frankentorch facade lives here, grep-enforceable), ftts-cli (cli_main + two thin bin shims: franken_tts and ftts), ftts-conformance (dev-only member holding integration tests/benches/fuzz — a virtual workspace root does NOT auto-discover tests/).

DELIBERATE ABSENCES: NO database history, NO sync subcommands — stateless by default (synthesized texts + voices are sensitive data); opt-in traces only. Deps: frankentorch (kernel level only), asupersync (orchestration only), no rusqlite ever.

EXIT: builds green on linux x86-64/arm64, darwin x86-64/arm64, windows-msvc; robot schema/health/backends emit valid versioned JSON; empty pipeline skips-green without weights; scripts/check.sh is the one-command gate.

title: EPIC Phase 1: Exact safe forward (ConformanceExact)
description:
EPIC — Phase 1: Exact safe forward (ConformanceExact green end-to-end, BF16/f32, zero optimization).

WHY FIRST: correctness outranks speed, always (G1 > G2). This phase lands the ENTIRE forward pipeline code-first in safe Rust — text/prompt path (verbatim mode), talker with mRoPE, the SEQUENTIAL 15-step microdecoder (the honest baseline every later lever must match bit-for-bit or distributionally), streaming+offline codec, both cloning paths (x-vector via ECAPA speaker encoder; ICL via codec encoder + transcript), two-level sampler with canonical greedy mode — then proves it seam-by-seam against oracle fixtures (teacher-forced per talker layer, per microdecoder depth, per codec block).

KEY RULES: implement from the extracted spec, never line-by-line from Python; weights stay ZERO-COPY BF16-resident (widen at the accessor — no whole-model f32 expansion; the text embedding alone is ~622 MB); rayon parallelism is fine here (KernelTeam comes in Phase 3); every module carries unit tests with detailed logging; streaming==batch is a standing gate from day one (chunked codec decode with ring buffers must equal offline decode of the same tokens).

EXIT: ConformanceExact ladder green end-to-end (L0 front-end exact -> L1 per-op -> L2 per-layer/depth/block -> L3 logits argmax-exact where oracle reproduces itself -> L4 codec-token stream exact under canonical greedy -> L5 audio per the pre-committed OQ-12 fork); WeightsManifest census passes; both clone modes produce reference-matching outputs.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
TRUTH PACK CORRECTION C-1 (from frankentts-t-pin-sources-b2u) — LOAD-BEARING, changes the per-frame execution graph.

Plan §2.1's pseudocode ends at 'enqueue the 16-code frame for the codec'. The pinned source
(snapshots/gh/qwen_tts/core/models/modeling_qwen3_tts.py:1671-1692) does two more things per frame:

  1. All 16 code embeddings are SUMMED into the talker's NEXT-step input:
       inputs_embeds = cat([talker_emb(code0)] + [depth_emb[i](code_{i+1}) for i in 0..14]).sum(1)
  2. A text hidden state is ADDED on top, one per frame:
       + trailing_text_hidden[:, generation_step]   if generation_step < len(trailing_text_hidden)
       + tts_pad_embed                              otherwise

Consequence: the text stream is consumed ONE HIDDEN PER FRAME, interleaved with audio generation —
it is NOT a prefill-only prefix. Any forward that treats text as fully consumed at prefill desyncs
after frame 1. Also adds a 16-way embedding-sum + add to the hot loop op set.

Full detail + citations: docs/truth-pack/FACT_DISPOSITIONS.md (C-1).

title: EPIC Phase 2: Canonical Q8 artifact (.fttsq/.fttspack)
description:
EPIC — Phase 2: Canonical Q8 artifact (.fttsq + .fttspack + staged quantization).

STRATEGY (START WITH INT8, NOT Q4 — nominal bit width is not a performance metric): per-output-channel INT8 weights on talker + microdecoder GEMMs; dynamic INT8 activations where the hardware path is genuinely fast; INT32 accumulation with fused requant; HIGH PRECISION kept for all norms, sampling-logits boundaries, RVQ codec codebooks, speaker-conditioning path, codec-sensitive layers. Codec at Q8 with high-precision codebooks (the upstream GGML maintainer's converged policy — validate exact set via OQ-13). EMBEDDINGS ARE DIFFERENTIATED: the ~622 MB cold text embedding is a legitimate separately-gated Q8 experiment (row-wise cold access); acoustic RVQ codebooks stay high-precision. Per-depth precision on the 15 microdecoder depths is a first-class axis.

ARTIFACT SPLIT (load-bearing): .fttsq = immutable canonical portable model (logical tensors, recipe, manifest, per-section SHA-256, license/NOTICE, NO machine-specific tiling; ~1.6 GB-class with BF16 text embedding, ~1.3 GB if Q8-embedding experiment passes) vs .fttspack = regenerable per-machine execution cache (packed layouts, microdecoder hot pack, autotuned KernelPlan; keyed by model hash + kernel ABI + CPU + ISA + packing version + quant mode + autotune hash). Conversion is STREAMING and bounded-memory (never load whole BF16 model into RAM widened to f32). Runtime quantization ships FIRST; the converter reuses the identical quantizer function so artifact==runtime is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION.

EXIT: staged levers (talker -> microdecoder -> heads gated -> codec Q8) each pass ConformanceExact + ProductionQuality gates; hardened parsers fuzzed; round-trip determinism proven.

title: EPIC Phase 3A: Microdecoder engine (ResidualCodeDecoder + FrankenMTP)
description:
EPIC — Phase 3A: The Microdecoder Engine (ResidualCodeDecoder + FrankenMTP). THE FLAGSHIP EPIC and the critical path of the whole project.

WHY IT IS THE FLAGSHIP: per 80 ms frame the 5-layer microdecoder runs 15 SEQUENTIAL times with per-depth embeddings and per-depth 2048-way heads — ~1.21 GB/frame of the ~1.65 GB sequential baseline (12.5 x 15 x 5 = 937.5 microdecoder-layer evaluations per second of speech vs 350 talker-layer evaluations). The official implementation runs this through full generic HF generation machinery; a fixed-topology zero-allocation engine is the single most model-specific thing this project builds.

CONTENT: the ResidualCodeDecoder (fixed 15-step loop, compile-time shapes, per-frame-reset tiny KV, precomputed 16-position RoPE table, direct per-depth embed/head indexing, no allocation, no generic machinery); the ~110 MB-class MTP hot pack in .fttspack (cache residency, operationally measured); the seq-16 verification kernel (a custom multi-head-per-position engine, NOT a stock LM pass); FrankenMTP drafter #1 (previous-frame residuals + transition stats — no training needed) with greedy-mode exactness by construction; the named speculative-sampling algorithm for sampled mode (OQ-19); the AF-3 e-value reliability monitor (kill-switch; NOT an exactness substitute); MTP-first Q4 experiments.

CLAIM TIERS (pre-written so a sour OQ-5 cannot collapse the epic): Tier 1 (training-mode forward mask/distribution-equivalent to the 15-step loop) = exact verifier, strict token identity + sampled distributional exactness claimable. Tier 2 (not equivalent) = approximate draft assistance, Contract-B-only claims, AF-3 always on, sequential path stays the only exact mode.

EXIT: sequential engine at/near its roofline per -1B; FrankenMTP verdict (keep with tier claim / revert with ledger entry); every lever behind FTTS_* kill-switches with parity receipts.

title: EPIC Phase 3B: Talker and prefill engine
description:
EPIC — Phase 3B: Talker & prefill engine.

SCOPE: the 28-layer talker on the KernelTeam as a persistent dispatch-free loop (per-layer fused pass 1: norm -> QKV -> QK-Norm(if OQ-3 confirms) -> mRoPE -> GQA attention -> O-proj -> residual; pass 2: norm -> gate||up -> SiLU-mul -> down -> residual with the corrected two-pass norm->quant fusion); exact-shape int8 GEMV kernels (1024/2048/3072/128 shapes all tile cleanly); the register-blocked tiled SMMLA/VNNI prefill GEMM (the "wedge" kernel frankentorch names but does not ship); the text projection MLP (2048->2048->1024 SiLU) in the prefill path; prompt partial evaluation + .ftvoice-cache static-prefix KV reuse (cache ONLY the maximal prefix proven independent of target text per OQ-10); long-context KV layout + admission integration.

KEY NUMBERS: talker body ~440 MB Q8/frame; q_proj 1024->2048, o_proj 2048->1024, MLP 1024->3072; worst-case i32 accumulation at K=3072 (U8S8 <= ~99.5M, >=21x headroom — proof obligation in shipped selftest). TTFA is dominated by this epic's prefill path plus the first codec packet — it is the interactive profile's critical path per the -1B ranking.

EXIT: fused talker loop bit-identical to the Phase-1 reference; prefill at/near roofline; norm->quant fusion proven byte-identity-preserving; voice-cache prefix reuse proven equal to full prefill (metamorphic gate).

title: EPIC Phase 3C: Codec and streaming engine
description:
EPIC — Phase 3C: Codec & streaming engine.

WHY CO-EQUAL: many local TTS ports optimize the language model then discover the codec dominates end-to-end latency. Our codec (speech tokenizer decoder) is ~291 MB Q8 community-measured: 8 transformer-like layers (hidden 512, 16 heads x head_dim 64 — attention width 1024 = 2x hidden, same wider-than-hidden signature as the talker; sliding window 72), causal convs, upsample rates [8,5,4,3] (product 480, x4 base hop = 1920 samples per 12.5 Hz frame at 24 kHz — exact hop math confirmed by OQ-7).

CONTENT: stateful causal-conv ring buffers (receptive-field-sized, preallocated, state across chunks); fused conv+bias+norm+activation; specialized small attention at the exact codec shape; NO im2col materialization (direct conv loops at small fixed shapes); streaming upsampling writing directly into the output PCM buffer; distinct encode/decode builds (synthesis artifacts need not carry encoder machinery); packet adaptivity (1/2/4/auto frames — official stack uses 4-frame 320 ms packets; packet size is an execution-policy parameter, never silently equated with the 80 ms model frame); cancellation still checked every talker frame regardless of packet size.

STANDING GATE: streaming == offline decode of the same token stream, bit-identical target (same ops, same order) — ring-buffer state correctness is an e-process invariant in the gauntlet, plus chunk-boundary fuzzing and sustained streaming tests with backpressure/cancellation semantics.

EXIT: codec at/near roofline; packet autotuning wired to profiles; streaming==offline proof green; sustained tests green.

title: EPIC Phase 3D: Server throughput (continuous batching)
description:
EPIC — Phase 3D: Server throughput (continuous batching on high-core AMD).

THE INSIGHT: N isolated per-stream engines reread the same weights N times. A central frame scheduler batches the talker step across all ready streams (GEMV -> GEMM, weights read once), then batches EACH microdecoder depth 0..14 across streams (valid because streams are independent; each stream's depth-d token depends only on its OWN depth-(d-1)), then batches/pipelines codec packets — preserving every utterance's autoregressive dependency while amortizing every matrix read. This is the primary throughput axis on Threadripper/EPYC.

CONTENT: the frame/depth batching scheduler; the RAGGED FrankenMTP x batching joint design (under speculation streams reject at different depths — candidate policies: pad-and-mask cohorts, cohort splitting by accept depth, dual-lane scheduler with verify lane + sequential-repair lane, per-cohort re-drafting; ONE scheduler design shared with Phase 3A, not two independent diagrams); NUMA-local weight packs + CCD-aware affinity; admission control + queueing policy + the capacity certificate; AF-5 USL sweeps feeding pool_sizing tables and N-bucket KernelTeam partition rebind rules.

OWNERSHIP INVARIANT: the batching scheduler IS the engine's single parallel owner — multi-stream inside ONE fan-out, never N concurrent fan-outs; fttsd admission rides the same capacity model.

METRICS (headline): aggregate RTF (generated-audio-seconds per wall-clock second per socket), streams/socket, p95 admission-to-first-packet queueing latency under load, joules per generated minute.

title: EPIC Phase 4: The voice compiler
description:
EPIC — Phase 4: The Voice Compiler (enrollment as the project's SECOND THESIS).

PITCH: ftts enroll compiles messy real-world recordings into a reproducible, scored, portable voice asset. Reference-preparation quality often buys more perceived clone quality than another 15 percent of kernel speed — continuation-style cloners reproduce defects in the prompt recording (documented by Pocket upstream; assume Qwen shares the failure mode), so the tool must say so BEFORE the user discovers it in output.

CONTENT: automatic reference-segment discovery (VAD -> reject overlap/multi-speaker -> score clipping/SNR/reverb/music/stationarity -> phonetic coverage from transcript -> select candidate 3-12 s segments -> synthesize a fixed audition set from each -> rank objectively + optional listener preference -> preserve chosen segment AND alternatives in the enrollment report); ICL as the quality default (modes: quality=transcript-backed ICL, quick=x-vector-only with upstream-documented possible quality reduction, auto=ICL when transcript verifies else x-vector WITH WARNING — never presented as interchangeable equals); transcript verification (duration consistency, alignment confidence, omission/repetition detection, external ASR plugin contract — the shipping binary contains NO ASR); multi-reference selection-BEFORE-averaging; AF-4 formal treatment (submodular segment/multi-ref selection + attribute->quality loss model calibrated on the audition benchmark; fallback whole-file enrollment).

ARTIFACTS: portable .ftvoice (identity data + provenance + CONSENT ATTESTATION + reproducible preprocessing recipe; profiles portable/private/minimal) vs derived .ftvoice-cache (recomputable prompt/KV caches keyed by voice-recipe hash + model hash + prompt-builder version + streaming mode + quant recipe + math mode + engine ABI).

ETHICS (doctrine 10): no acquisition features, consent recorded, upstream watermark preserved (OQ-8).

title: EPIC Phase 5: Structural compression + lab track
description:
EPIC — Phase 5: Structural compression + the franken_tts_lab track (the full hierarchical-AR assault).

SCOPE RELAXATION (deliberate, fenced): the SHIPPING runtime stays inference-only, but this lab track may do model surgery targeted at the 15-step microdecoder monster: drafter distillation (including oracle residual-trajectory distillation — teacher-forced residual trajectories from the pinned oracle are FREE supervision), 15 parallel residual heads off the talker hidden state, cross-frame residual dynamics beyond prev-frame copy, block drafts of 3/5 with tree verify, joint talker->residual conditioning compression, adaptive/depth-conditional early exit, predictor pruning, per-depth precision via AF-1, talker Q4 if still worthwhile after MTP-first results, and TALKER-LEVEL SPECULATION as the sibling epic (after the residual layer is won, the talker still streams ~440 MB/frame forever — dual-level speculation over the whole hierarchical stack).

LAB -> RUNTIME ABI (so wins land as product, not notebooks): draft/surgery models ship as versioned .fttsdraft artifacts beside .fttsq — format-versioned, compatibility-keyed to model + engine ABI, kill-switched, parsed by the same hardened ftts-artifacts machinery.

QUALITY LAW: every lab output re-enters ONLY through the full verification gates, with SURGERY-SPECIFIC canaries (high-frequency loss, identity, sibilance under shallow/adaptive residual depth) — G1 over G2 applies to surgery doubly. If the 12Hz long-form drift gate failed AND a cloning-capable 25Hz Base exists, the 25Hz document-mode engine runs here as its own epic (predefined evidence trigger; dual-rate product).

title: EPIC Phase 6: Metal productization (conditional)
description:
EPIC — Phase 6: Metal productization (conditional on the -1B spike).

ENTRY CONDITION: only if the Phase -1B Metal microdecoder spike answered YES to "can a persistent Metal kernel/command-graph run the 15 residual steps including sampling and KV updates without 15 host round trips?" A negative spike verdict validly ended this path already.

PRE-STATED FULL-PATH CONTRACT (so Metal becomes a second full path, not a residual-only toy): (1) integer cross-backend contract — int8 x int8 -> i32 with post-accumulation scales gives EXACT CPU<->GPU equality regardless of accumulation order; (2) talker/codec co-residency plan alongside the persistent command-graph microdecoder; (3) CPU-fallback invariants — CPU stays the default product, every Metal path has a CPU twin, the shipped selftest covers both; (4) install-time CPU-vs-Metal benchmark policy per chip/quant/prompt-length/concurrency.

EVIDENCE BASIS: M5-class fused INT8 Metal precedent (Draw Things: fused dynamic-quant INT8 matmul 1.61-1.87x over FP16; INT8 attention 1.24-1.41x over Metal FlashAttention — image-model numbers establishing the mechanism, not our targets). CUDA sits behind Metal entirely. Negative verdicts at any point validly end the epic with a ledger entry.

title: EPIC Phase 7: Certify + ship
description:
EPIC — Phase 7: Certify + ship.

CONTENT: release certification via the /running-the-gauntlet-on-your-rust-port machinery — three pillars (performance / conformance / surface parity), no victory-on-one-while-another-regresses; conformal lower-bound release ratchet (ship decisions use the LOWER bound, never point estimates); e-processes (anytime-valid) over the standing invariants: streaming==batch, admission-before-allocation, i32-overflow at census worst-case K, determinism scope, SIMD==scalar; >=10 convergence rounds with >=2-clean-round tail; skip-honest ladder receipts (a skipped rung is NEVER mistaken for green).

RELEASE MECHANICS: 5-target build matrix (linux x86-64/arm64, darwin x86-64/arm64, windows-msvc); one self-contained binary per target (no Python, no foreign ML/DSP runtime, no C++ ABI, no non-system shared libs; tiny audited OS-interface islands for mmap/madvise/affinity are fine); install.sh + checksums; DISTRIBUTION PROOFS: convert byte-parity vs published artifact hash, clean-cache pull + one real synthesis per artifact; runtime selftest re-proves dispatched-kernel==scalar-oracle + overflow rows on the END USER'S silicon; sustained-thermal scorecard row (30-minute run — a turbo-window laptop number is not an interactive-TTS claim); Apache-2.0 attribution/NOTICE embedded in artifacts and --version.

Optional post-v1 companion: fttsd (OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint) as a separate binary riding the 3D capacity model — HTTP concerns never enter the core crates.

title: EPIC Verification infrastructure (contracts + listening + reliability)
description:
EPIC — Verification infrastructure (the two conformance contracts + listening protocol + reliability gates). Cross-cutting: this infra is INDEPENDENTLY REUSABLE, which is why it gets its own beads (per policy, implementation issues otherwise own their test criteria).

THE CENTRAL INSIGHT (v2): the official model SAMPLES at both autoregressive levels (talker T0.9/k50/rep1.05; residual T0.9/k50 — read from generation_config), so one ladder cannot serve two masters: a tiny legitimate logit perturbation can flip a token and diverge the whole sequence with zero perceptual harm. Split: Contract A ConformanceExact (teacher-forced activations/logits per talker layer + per microdecoder depth + per codec block; canonical greedy generation; exact ids; codec decode of fixed tokens; scalar==SIMD; cached==uncached; streaming==offline; the kernel-development ladder) vs Contract B ProductionQuality (teacher-forced distributional metrics: logit KL/JS, top-k overlap, reference rank, first-divergence distributions; PLUS free-running metrics under the production sampler: WER, repeated/skipped-word rate, stop-token errors, identity, prosody, long-form drift, listening equivalence; multi-seed paired-text rank statistics — never single-seed A/B; token equality is a diagnostic here, NOT the shipping gate).

ALSO IN THIS EPIC: the operationalized listening protocol (ABX identity, MUSHRA-style naturalness, TOST equivalence bounds with PREDEFINED margins per metric family, hierarchical analysis, canary-axis tail reporting, CI-nightly-vs-release automation boundary, AF-2 CVaR as a named ship-gate bit); metamorphic + golden suites; fuzzing; reliability gates (resource admission, runtime health watchdogs, streaming failure semantics).

title: [-1A] Integrated execution census generator + CI drift guard
description:
Finish the integration work split out of frankentts-t-census-44a.

DONE WHEN:
- A checked-in generator derives a machine-readable execution census from the pinned model config plus the already-pinned OQ-2 tensor inventory and OQ-7 codec facts, with no manually copied numeric rows.
- The committed census enumerates tensor shapes/dtypes/bytes, activation rails, KV footprints by duration, codec ring-buffer sizes from receptive fields, the microdecoder hot-working-set bytes as distinct traffic and footprint values, and the i32 overflow K/headroom table including the codec binding K=7168 row.
- A CI drift guard fails when the pinned input/config changes without regenerated census output.
- The published hot-working-set value is referenced by the Phase 3A hot-pack work and the cost graph / overflow-proof consumers continue to depend on this bead.

Already-landed inputs retained as authority: OQ-2 generator + TENSOR_INVENTORY.json (26b0bbe) and OQ-7 codec receptive-field/overflow facts (d46db67). This bead replaces only the unlanded integrated generator/guard/reference exit criteria.
close_reason: Generator + census + drift guard landed (e590490). scripts/generate_execution_census.py derives every row from pinned inputs only (TENSOR_INVENTORY.json + the two pinned configs); no numeric row is transcribed from prose. Output docs/truth-pack/EXECUTION_CENSUS.json enumerates per-component tensor shapes/dtypes/bytes, activation rails, talker KV by duration, codec ring-buffer sizes from computed receptive fields, the microdecoder hot working set as DISTINCT footprint (142.2 MB Q8) and traffic (1.24 GB/frame) values, and the i32 overflow K/headroom table including the K=7168 decode-path row. Drift guard is a check.sh stage and was PROVEN, not asserted: clean -> tampered exits 1 -> regenerated -> clean. Cross-check: independently reproduces the OQ-7 hand derivation exactly (579.3796875 total left-context frames, 11.3796875 conv-only, 2.25 MiB live codec KV). Two corrections forced by the derivation and propagated to consumers: (1) hot working set is 142.2 MB Q8, not the plan's ~110 MB-class -- plan 2.6 lists the 15 per-depth embeddings then omits their 31.5 MB from its own total; filed on b-residency-oq18-jzx since it changes the residency question. (2) The binding overflow row must be reported twice -- global K=8192 (enrollment-only Mimi encoder, headroom 8.09x) vs decode-path K=7168 (headroom 9.25x); my earlier OQ-7 claim that 7168 was 'the project's binding worst case' was right for decode and wrong for the checkpoint; filed on p2-overflow-proofs-0o1. Gates: validate_repo 9 rules OK, drift guard clean, ubs --diff/--staged 0; no Rust changed.

title: [VER] Wire health detectors into the decode seams + robot health events
description:
The runtime-health detectors landed under frankentts-v-reliability-d65 (3627c58, crates/ftts-core/src/health.rs) are implemented and unit-tested but have NOTHING TO OBSERVE YET: Phase 0 has no decode loop. This bead calls them from the real seams as those seams land.

WHAT:
1. NumericGuard at the four seams (talker logits, microdecoder logits per depth, codec output, PCM) once each exists, honouring SeamPolicy from config.
2. ProgressWatchdog + RunawayDetector inside the frame loop; SilenceDetector on the PCM path.
3. check_stop_consistency at the point StopReason is decided, before it is reported.
4. KernelSelector::on_selftest_failure wired to the shipped selftest (frankentts-p2-overflow-proofs-0o1), so an ISA kernel that fails demotes to the certified scalar baseline in production, not just in principle.
5. ThermalReporter fed by the sustained-run harness.
6. ROBOT SIDE: HealthEvent::Violation must reach the robot NDJSON stream. ftts-cli/src/robot.rs already catalogues a health event; add the violation fields there, re-freeze tests/fixtures/robot_schema_v1.json via the documented cp path, and emit from the observer. HealthEvent::as_str() and HealthViolation::as_str() already supply the stable wire strings.
7. ftts-cli 'say --check' still uses its own scaffold admission_plan(), whose text says 'model-specific KV and memory admission is pending the V_REL engine'. That engine now exists (ftts_core::admission) — the CLI preflight should call it so the CLI and the engine cannot disagree about whether a request fits.

WHY SEPARATE: every item needs a component that does not exist yet, or touches ftts-cli (a different lane). The mechanisms, their thresholds, and their failure-injection tests are done and green; this is integration.

DONE WHEN: each detector is called from its real seam; a forced NaN/stall/runaway/silence in an integration test produces the corresponding HealthEvent in BOTH the observer and robot NDJSON; the CLI preflight and the engine produce the same admission decision for the same request.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
cc_1: increment 1 landed but UNVERIFIED — committed as 5535911 (swept in by another agent between my git add and git commit; content confirmed present in HEAD).

IMPLEMENTED (2 of 7 items — the only two that CAN be done now):

comments.author: jemanuel

title: [CI] Phase-0 exit criterion 'builds green on all 5 targets' has no enforcing mechanism
close_reason: Machine-enforced in scripts/check.sh stage 5b (b741bc4): all five release targets type-checked inside the one blocking job, skip-honest (a missing std is a named SKIP, never green) and hard-fail in CI via FTTS_REQUIRE_ALL_TARGETS=1 with all five stds installed by the gate job. Deliberately NOT done by making the workflow's cross job blocking -- its own comment records the measured runner-starvation reason (run 31123043545 queued 9m+ on a free-plan cap shared across every Dicklesworthstone repo), and starving the blocking gate to prove an advisory cross-check would trade an enforceable criterion for an unobservable one. VERIFIED: the stage ran under FTTS_REQUIRE_ALL_TARGETS=1 and passed all five (902s); each target also corroborated independently (aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin 9m32s, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 1m18s, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc 5m21s, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu via the stage -- rch's workers lack that std and produced a misleading E0463 that is a provisioning artifact, not a target break).

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
Found while verifying the Phase 0 epic exit gate (frankentts-ep-phase0-skeleton-sfb), which requires
'builds green on linux x86-64/arm64, darwin x86-64/arm64, windows-msvc'.

The workflow has exactly the right matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml:140-145 lists all five targets),
but the job that runs it cannot satisfy the criterion as written:

  line 124-135  job 'cross'
  line 128-ish  continue-on-error: true      -> a target break NEVER fails the run
  line 136      if: github.event_name != 'push'  -> it does not run on main pushes at all

So on main, the five-target check is both absent and non-blocking. It runs on PRs and nightly, where
a failure is still advisory. This is a deliberate choice by p0-ci-083 -- the workflow comment says
'ADVISORY ... without blocking a merge on a platform we do not yet ship', which is a reasonable
velocity trade -- but it is in direct tension with a Phase-0 EXIT criterion that says those builds
must be green. An exit gate that nothing enforces is not a gate.

Compounding it, and tracked separately as frankentts-nlb: no CI run has ever completed. 'gh run list'
shows every run from the last 3+ hours queued or pending, so there is no green evidence from ANY job,
advisory or not.

DECIDE ONE (this is a scoping call for the orchestrator, not a code fix):
  (a) Make cross blocking on main for the five targets -- honours the plan text, costs runner time
      the project currently does not have (see nlb).
  (b) Keep it advisory and AMEND the Phase-0 exit criterion to say what is actually enforced, e.g.
      'host target green + five-target cross-check advisory-green on the most recent nightly'. Honest
      and cheap, but it is a plan change and should be recorded as one, not absorbed silently.
  (c) Narrow Phase 0 to the targets we actually ship now and move the rest to p7-release-t7o, which
      already owns cross-platform release proofs.

Until one is chosen and satisfied, the Phase 0 epic cannot close on criterion 1. I verified the host
target (aarch64-apple-darwin) green locally; the other four have no evidence of any kind.
